Client-Server Architecture: The server is authoritative: validates actions, simulates world state. Clients send input, receive updates. Thin client vs thick client. Tick rate, bandwidth, and latency tradeoffs.
Peer-to-Peer & Relay: P2P: players connect directly—low latency, complex NAT traversal (STUN/TURN/ICE). Relay: server forwards traffic—simpler NAT handling, adds latency. Rollback netcode for fighting games.
Netcode & State Synchronization: Authoritative server sends world state deltas. Client-side prediction hides latency. Entity interpolation smooths other players. Snapshot compression (bitpacking, delta encoding).
Lag Compensation & Prediction: Client predicts own movement immediately (no input lag). Server rewinds time for hit detection (lag compensation). Extrapolation estimates positions of others. Reconciliation corrects prediction errors.
Rollback Netcode: Fighting game technique: simulate future frames, roll back when server disagrees. Saves snapshots for rollback. Input delay + prediction for responsive feel. GGPO-style implementation.
Matchmaking & Lobbies: Matchmaking: skill-based (ELO, TrueSkill), ping-based, party support. Lobbies: pre-game rooms with player slots, ready states, chat. Steamworks / Epic Online Services for cross-platform.
WebSocket & REST for Games: WebSocket: persistent full-duplex connection for real-time game data. REST: HTTP for authentication, leaderboards, store. gRPC / MessagePack for efficient binary protocols.
NAT Punchthrough & Relay Servers: NAT (Network Address Translation) blocks direct P2P connections. STUN: discover public IP/port. TURN: relay traffic when P2P fails. ICE: combine STUN/TURN candidates. Server relay for fallback.

Addressables: Unity's asset management system for loading/unloading assets at runtime. Async loading with async/await or callbacks. Remote content delivery (asset bundles from cloud). Dependency management and reference counting.

Cinemachine & Timeline: Cinemachine: intelligent camera system—virtual cameras, blends, noise (shaking), dolly tracks, 3rd-person follow, aiming dead zones. Timeline: cinematic sequence editor for cutscenes, camera cuts, animation tracks.
Burst Compiler & Jobs System: Burst: high-performance LLVM-based compiler that translates C# to highly optimized native code. Unity Jobs System: safe multithreading with JobHandle and dependency management. ParallelFor jobs.

Scriptable Objects Deep: ScriptableObjects as data containers: avoid MonoBehaviour overhead, enable asset-based architecture. Use for game events, item definitions, dialogue trees, level configs. Create asset at runtime with CreateInstance. Custom editors for inspector polish.

Scene Management & Multi-Scene: LoadSceneMode.Additive for multi-scene workflows (persistent managers, UI layer, gameplay levels). SceneManager events (sceneLoaded, activeSceneChanged). Addressables scene loading. DontDestroyOnLoad pattern. Editor tooling for multi-scene editing.
Custom Editor Tools: Unity Editor extending: CustomEditor, PropertyDrawer, EditorWindow, ScriptableWizard, Gizmos, MenuItem. IMGUI vs UI Toolkit for editor UI. SerializedObject/SerializedProperty introspection. Scene GUI for in-world editing handles.
NavMesh & AI Navigation: Unity AI Navigation: NavMesh baking, NavMeshAgent pathfinding, OffMeshLinks for gaps/jumps, NavMeshObstacle for dynamic obstacles. Agent avoidance (RVOS). NavMeshSurface, NavMeshLink, NavMeshModifier components.
VFX Graph: Unity Visual Effect Graph: GPU-accelerated particle systems, node-based graph editor. Event system, exposed properties for runtime control. Capacities (particle limits). Integration with Shader Graph for custom blocks and outputs.

Blueprint vs C++ Deep: Blueprint: visual scripting, fast iteration, ideal for designers, slower at runtime (noding overhead). C++: performance-critical systems, engine extensions, complex algorithms. Best practice: C++ for base classes, Blueprint for gameplay.
Gameplay Ability System: GAS: robust ability framework for skills, buffs, cooldowns. Core: UAbilitySystemComponent, UGameplayAbility, UGameplayEffect, UAttributeSet. Supports stacking, tags, replication. Used in AAA shooters and RPGs.
Enhanced Input: UE5's Enhanced Input system replaces Action/Axis mappings. UInputAction with modifiers (deadzone, chorded) and triggers (pressed, held, double-tap). UInputMappingContext for context-sensitive bindings.
UMG Deep: Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG) for HUD and menus. Widget Blueprint: Canvas Panel, Horizontal/Vertical Box, Overlay. BindWidget for C++ access. Animations (widget animations). Retainer Box for render caching.
Niagara VFX: Niagara is UE's next-gen VFX system. Emitters with particle spawn/update/render stages. Modules for forces, noise, collisions. GPU particles for massive counts. Data interfaces for external data.
Chaos Physics: UE5's Chaos Physics replaces PhysX. Destructible meshes with fracture modes (Voronoi, clustered). Cloth simulation. Vehicle dynamics with modular suspension/engine/transmission. Custom constraints.
Control Rig & IK: Control Rig: procedural animation system within UE. Full-body IK with FABRIK solver. Aim constraints, multi-priority IK. Sequencer integration for cinematic rigging. Python scripting for automation.
GameplayTags & GameFeatures: GameplayTags: hierarchical tag system (Aura.Fire.Major). Fast, editor-managed. Used for state, interaction rules, ability blocking. GameFeatures: modular content plugins enabling/disabling entire systems.
World Partition & OFPA: UE5's World Partition system replaces level streaming. One File Per Actor (OFPA): each actor in its own package. World partition grid with streaming cells. Runtime loading/unloading based on player proximity. HLOD for distant meshes.
MetaSounds: UE5's high-performance audio system. Node-based graph: oscillators, envelopes, filters, delays, convolution reverb. Parameter control via Blueprint/C++ at audio rate. Real-time synthesis replacing legacy Sound Cues.
Animation Blueprint & State Machines: AnimBP: per-bone animation blending, state machines, blend spaces, aim offsets, layered blending. Cached pose for performance. Sub-anim instances for weapon/ability-specific animations. Root motion extraction.
Smart Objects & State Tree: Smart Objects: interactive world objects with behavior definitions (sit, lean, open). State Tree: hierarchical behavior tree with state transitions, conditions, and tasks. Lightweight, data-driven AI for smart interactions.
PCG Framework: Procedural Content Generation framework in UE5. Graph-based node system: terrain spawning, scatter, noise filtering, density mapping. Runtime and editor generation. Integration with World Partition and Landscape.
Mass Entity System & AI: UE5's Mass framework: data-oriented ECS for thousands of AI agents. Fragments (data), processors (logic), archetypes (composition). LOD system (full simulation → LOD → off-screen). Crowd avoidance, movement, AI sensory.

Game Loops & Architecture: The game loop is the heart of every game: input, update, render. Fixed timestep decouples simulation from framerate. Use accumulator pattern for fixed-update with variable rendering.
ECS (Entity-Component-System): ECS decouples data (components) from behavior (systems), iterated over entities (IDs). Cache-friendly, data-oriented design. Favors composition over inheritance.
Design Patterns in Games: Common patterns: Singleton (GameManager), Observer (events), Command (input buffering), Object Pool (bullets), State (AI), Flyweight (shared data). Use wisely—patterns solve problems, don't force them.
Game Feel & Juice: Juice is the extra polish: screen shake, particle bursts, tweening, sound cues, hit-stop, flash effects. These positive feedback loops make gameplay satisfying and responsive.
Feedback Loops: Positive loops amplify (snowballing—winner gets stronger), negative loops stabilize (rubber-banding—last place gets boost). Both used carefully to balance engagement and fairness.
Difficulty Curves: Difficulty should ramp gradually with optional plateaus. Player-skill vs challenge must stay in flow channel—too easy bores, too hard frustrates. Adaptive difficulty adjusts in real-time.
Game Economy & Balancing: Virtual economies manage resources (gold, XP, mana). Balance via tuning loops: playtest, gather data, adjust. Watch for inflation, grinding, and dominant strategies in multiplayer.
State Machines for Game Logic: Finite state machines model entity behavior. Each state has Enter/Update/Exit. Transitions triggered by events or conditions. Hierarchical FSM nests states for complexity.

Collision Detection — AABB & Circle: AABB (axis-aligned bounding box) is the fastest overlap test. Circle-circle uses distance vs radius sum. Broad-phase uses simple checks before narrow-phase.
Collision Detection — SAT & GJK: SAT (Separating Axis Theorem) checks all potential separating axes. GJK (Gilbert-Johnson-Keerthi) iteratively finds closest distance between convex shapes. EPA expands GJK for collision info.
Physics Integration (Euler, Verlet, RK4): Euler: simple but unstable. Verlet: excellent for springs/cloth (stores position, not velocity). RK4: 4th-order Runge-Kutta, most accurate for forces, used in scientific simulations.
Friction & Restitution: Friction opposes sliding (Coulomb model: static vs kinetic). Restitution (bounciness, 0–1) controls energy retained after collision. Combined via coefficient of restitution formula.
Joints & Constraints: Joints connect rigid bodies: revolute (hinge), prismatic (slider), distance (rod), spring, fixed. Constraints restrict degrees of freedom. Solved via iterative impulse solvers (PBD, sequential impulses).
Raycasting: Raycasting fires a ray and returns first intersected object. Used for shooting, line-of-sight, mouse picking. Möller–Trumbore algorithm for triangle intersection.
Spatial Partitioning: Partition space to avoid O(n²) checks. Grid: simple, good for uniform分布. Quadtree/Octree: recursive subdivision, adapts to density. BVH: bounding volume hierarchy for dynamic objects.
Physics Engine Architecture: Engines loop: broadphase (detect pairs), narrowphase (generate contacts), solve constraints, integrate. Common engines: Box2D, Bullet, PhysX, Jolt. Determinism matters for multiplayer.

Rendering Pipeline: The graphics pipeline transforms 3D data to pixels. Stages: vertex shader → tessellation → geometry → rasterization → fragment shader → output merger. Modern GPUs are massively parallel.
Shaders — Vertex & Fragment: Vertex shaders transform vertices and pass data. Fragment (pixel) shaders compute final color. GLSL/HLSL syntax. Input: attributes (per-vertex), uniforms (per-draw), varyings (interpolated).
Lighting Models: Lambertian diffuse: max(N·L, 0). Blinn-Phong adds specular: pow(N·H, shininess). PBR uses microfacet models (Cook-Torrance BRDF) with roughness/metalness for physically-based results.
Shadows: Shadow mapping: render depth from light's view, then sample during main pass. PCF (percentage-closer filtering) softens edges. Cascaded shadow maps split depth for large scenes.
Post-Processing: Full-screen passes applied after rendering: bloom (bright-pass + blur), tone-mapping (HDR to LDR), color grading, SSR (screen-space reflections), SSAO (ambient occlusion), motion blur.
GPU Instancing & Batching: Instancing renders many copies with one draw call—each instance has per-instance data (transform, color). Static batching merges static objects. Dynamic batching groups small meshes.
LODs (Level of Detail): Switch mesh complexity based on distance or screen-size. LOD 0 (full detail) near camera, LOD 1-3 further. Cross-fading or popping. Impostors (billboard textures) for extreme distance.
Culling (Frustum, Occlusion): Frustum culling: discard objects outside camera view frustum using plane tests. Occlusion culling: skip objects behind occluders. Hierarchical Z-buffer (Hi-Z) for GPU occlusion.

Audio Engines & Middleware: Audio engines manage playback, mixing, effects. Options: OpenAL (open-source), FMOD (popular in AAA), Wwise (full pipeline), Web Audio API (browser). Middleware handles platform differences.
3D Audio (Positional Audio): Position audio sources in 3D space using attenuation curves (linear, inverse, logarithmic). Listener has position/orientation. HRTF (head-related transfer function) for realistic spatialization.
DSP Effects: Digital Signal Processing: reverb (convolution or feedback delay), EQ (low/high/band-pass filters), chorus, flange, distortion, compressor. Graph of AudioNodes in Web Audio / audio middleware.
Sound Pooling: Pre-allocate audio instances to avoid garbage-collection hits. Pool returns a free source; if all in use, steal oldest or skip. Crucial for frequent sounds (footsteps, gunshots).
Music Systems: Dynamic music adapts to gameplay. Techniques: horizontal resequencing (swap sections), vertical layering (add/subtract layers), stingers (transition cues). MIDI vs audio stems.
FMOD / Wwise Basics: FMOD Studio: event-driven audio, parametric controls, real-time mixing. Wwise: full sound design pipeline with SoundBanks, RTPCs (real-time parameter controls), States, and Switches.
Adaptive Audio: Audio reacts to game state: combat intensity, health, speed, environment. Blend snapshots, adjust reverb zones, trigger stingers. Prevents audio fatigue and heightens immersion.

Vectors: Vectors represent positions, directions, velocities. Operations: add, subtract, scale, dot product (angle), cross product (perpendicular in 3D), normalize (unit length). Foundation of game math.
Matrices & Transforms: 4×4 matrices encode translation, rotation, scale. Matrix multiplication composes transforms. Model→World→View→Projection pipeline. Inverse matrix undoes transformation.
Quaternions: Quaternions represent rotation without gimbal lock. q = (cos(θ/2), sin(θ/2) * axis). Unit quaternion for rotation. Slerp for smooth interpolation. Multiply to compose rotations.
Interpolation (Lerp, Slerp, Easing): Lerp: linear interpolation (a + t*(b-a)). Slerp: spherical for quaternions. Easing functions: ease-in (quadratic), ease-out, ease-in-out, elastic, bounce. Used in animations and transitions.
Noise Functions: Perlin noise: smooth, gradient-based, lattice noise. Simplex noise: faster, fewer artifacts, scales to N-dimensions. Used for terrain, textures, procedural generation. Fractal Brownian Motion layers octaves.
Curves & Splines: Catmull-Rom: interpolates through control points (used for camera paths). Bézier: uses control points (Cubic: 4 points). Hermite: specifies tangents. NURBS: rational curves for CAD.
Trigonometry for Games: Sine/cosine for oscillating motion, circular movement, wave effects. Atan2 for angle between points. Used in aiming, field-of-view checks, projectile trajectories, Lissajous patterns.
Coordinate Spaces: Local (object) → World → View (camera) → Clip → Screen. Normalized device coordinates (NDC): [-1,1]. UV/texel coordinates: [0,1] for textures. Proper transforms prevent visual glitches.

Finite State Machines: FSM: entity is in exactly one state at a time. Transitions defined by events/conditions. Simple, predictable AI. HFSM (Hierarchical) nests states for reuse. Drawback: becomes unwieldy with many states.
Behavior Trees: Tree of tasks: Sequence (all succeed), Selector (first success), Condition, Action, Decorator (invert, repeat, cooldown). Blackboard stores shared data. More modular than FSM.
GOAP (Goal-Oriented Action Planning): AI picks actions based on goals and world state. Planner searches for cheapest action sequence achieving the goal. Used in F.E.A.R. Actions have preconditions and effects.
Utility AI: Each action gets a score based on context (distance, health, ammo). Highest-scoring action executes. Scores computed via response curves (linear, logistic, exponential). Smooth, tunable, realistic.
A* Pathfinding: A* finds shortest path using g(n) (cost from start) + h(n) (heuristic to goal). Guarantees optimal path with admissible heuristic. Open set (priority queue), closed set (visited).
Dijkstra & JPS Pathfinding: Dijkstra: A* with h(n)=0, finds shortest to all nodes. JPS (Jump Point Search): speeds up A* on uniform-cost grids by jumping over empty areas. Symmetry reduction for open spaces.
Navmesh: Navigation mesh: walkable surface represented as convex polygons. A* on navmesh graph, then funnel algorithm for path straightening. Handles any-angle movement, dynamic obstacles.
Flocking & Steering Behaviors: Boids model: separation (avoid neighbors), alignment (match velocity), cohesion (move to center). Steering behaviors: seek, flee, pursue, evade, wander, obstacle avoidance. Combined via weighted blending.

Skeletal Animation: Mesh bound to a bone hierarchy (skeleton). Each vertex weighted to 1-4 bones (skinning). Animation stores per-bone transforms at keyframes. Interpolated and applied as matrix palette.
Blend Trees: Blend between multiple animations based on parameters. 1D blend: idle→walk→run by speed. 2D blend: direction + speed. Freeform Cartesian for complex spaces. Additive blends for layers.
Inverse Kinematics (IK): IK computes joint angles to reach a target position. CCD (Cyclic Coordinate Descent): iterative joint rotation. FABRIK: forward-and-backward reaching. Two-bone IK: analytic solution for arms/legs.
Blend Shapes (Morph Targets): Store multiple vertex positions for the same mesh. Interpolate between shapes for facial animation, morphing. Basis shape + delta arrays. Weighted combination for complex expressions.
Animation State Machines: Graph of animation states with transitions, blend times, and conditions. Parameters drive transitions (bool, float, int, trigger). Cross-fade between animations prevents popping.
Animation Rigging: Constraint-based system layered on top of animation: aim constraints (look-at), parent constraints, chain IK, twist correction. Used for procedural adjustments without modifying original clips.
Motion Matching: Match live pose + trajectory to database of animations. Search for nearest neighbor by feature vector (root velocity, foot positions). Blend at transitions. Used in The Last of Us, Assassin's Creed.

Input Abstraction: Abstract input layer decouples game logic from hardware. Query actions (Jump, Shoot) instead of keys. Allows swapping keyboard/gamepad/touch without game changes.
Input Rebinding: Allow players to reassign keys/buttons at runtime. Store bindings in config file. Detect conflicts, validate (ensure at least one binding per action). Present UI with waiting-for-input prompt.
Action Mapping: Map abstract actions to concrete inputs. Digital (button press) vs Analog (stick, trigger). Value: 0/1 for digital, -1..1 for axis. Dead zones, inversion, sensitivity curves per action.
Gamepad Input: Gamepad API provides sticks, buttons, triggers (pressure-sensitive), and rumble. Standard mapping: left stick move, right stick look, A/B/X/Y, shoulder buttons. XInput (Windows) / GameController (macOS/Linux).
Touch & Gesture Input: Touch events: touchstart, touchmove, touchend. Multi-touch tracking via identifier. Gestures: tap, double-tap, swipe, pinch (zoom), rotate, long-press. Gesture recognizers abstract raw touch.
Gyroscope & Motion Sensors: DeviceOrientation/Motion APIs provide alpha (compass), beta (tilt front-back), gamma (tilt left-right). Acceleration with/without gravity. Used for tilt controls, VR head tracking, step counting.
Haptics & Accessibility: Haptic feedback: gamepad rumble (continuous/impulse), phone vibration. Accessibility: color-blind modes, subtitle sizing, remappable controls, auto-aim, slow-motion assists, single-switch input.

Perlin & Simplex Noise: Perlin noise: lattice-based gradient noise (Ken Perlin, 1985). Simplex noise: faster, better isotropy, scales to any dimension. Fractal noise (FBM) layers octaves for natural-looking terrain.
Cellular Automata: Grid of cells with states evolving by rules. Conway's Game of Life: birth on 3 neighbors, death on <2 or >3. Used for cave generation (cave-like automata with B678/S345678 rules).
Wave Function Collapse: WFC generates tile-based patterns matching input examples. Start with maximum entropy (superposition), observe (collapse) lowest-entropy cell, propagate constraints. Used for infinite worlds, architecture, puzzles.
L-Systems: Lindenmayer systems: recursive string rewriting for plants, fractals. Axiom + production rules. Each symbol is a turtle graphics command (F=forward, +=turn left, -=turn right, [=push, ]=pop).
Dungeon Generation: BSP (Binary Space Partition): recursively split rooms. Random walk: drunkard's walk for cave-like tunnels. Prefab-based: stitch hand-designed rooms. Delaunay + MST for connecting rooms with corridors.
Terrain Generation: Heightmap generation via FBM noise. Erosion simulation (hydraulic, thermal) adds realism. Biomes determined by temperature + humidity noise. GPU tessellation for dynamic detail.
Procedural Textures: Generate textures mathematically: Voronoi (cellular), checkerboard, marble (sine + noise), wood (concentric rings), brick (tiling patterns). No external assets needed—infinite resolution.

CPU Profiling: Instrument your game to find hot spots. Frame time budget: 16ms (60fps). Tools: Chrome DevTools (web), Tracy (native), Unreal Insights, Unity Profiler. Identify dominant systems (physics, AI, rendering).
GPU Profiling & Optimization: RenderDoc, NVIDIA Nsight, AMD Radeon GPU Profiler. Analyze draw calls, shader complexity, bandwidth. Bottlenecks: vertex-bound, pixel-bound, bandwidth-bound. Reduce overdraw, optimize shaders.
การจัดการหน่วยความจำ: Avoid GC spikes: object pooling, structs (value types), pre-allocate arrays. Memory fragmentation. Asset lifetime management. Leak detection. Addressable assets for streaming.
Draw Call Optimization: Each draw call has CPU overhead. Batching: static (combine meshes), dynamic (GPU instancing). Reduce material changes (sort by shader/texture). Texture atlasing. SRP Batcher (Unity).
Asset Streaming & Bundling: Stream assets in background while game runs. Priority loading (nearby first). Texture mipmap streaming. Asset bundles for DLC/patches. Compression: ASTC (mobile), BC7 (desktop), Oodle.
Threading & Job Systems: Main thread handles rendering, game logic offloaded to worker threads. Job system: small, independent work units scheduled across cores. Task graph for dependencies. Fiber-based scheduling.
Level-of-Detail Strategies: Geometric LOD: swap mesh complexity by distance. Shader LOD: simpler shaders for distant objects. Texture LOD: mipmaps. Animation LOD: lower update rate for distant characters. Impostor billboards.

Binary vs JSON vs XML: JSON: human-readable, flexible, larger size. Binary: compact, fast to parse, fixed schema. Protocol Buffers / MessagePack: cross-language, version-tolerant. XML: verbose, used in legacy formats.
Save Game Data Design: Save format: versioned for forward compatibility. Separate player data from world state. Auto-save on checkpoints. Manifest file for save listing. Corruption prevention: atomic writes, CRC checksums.
Cloud Saves & Sync: Steam Cloud, Epic Cloud Save, Google Play Cloud, iCloud. Sync on close, download on launch. Conflict resolution: last-write-wins, merge strategies. Offline queue with deferred upload.
Compression for Game Data: Deflate/gzip: general purpose, good compression. LZ4: extremely fast decompression. Oodle Kraken (used in AAA). Texture compression: BCn, ASTC, ETC2. Mesh compression: Draco, meshoptimizer.
Config Files & Settings: Separate game settings (video, audio, controls) from save data. INI, JSON, TOML, or binary config. Detect GPU/display on first launch. Cloud sync settings across devices.
Auto-Save & Checkpoints: Save at safe points: level transitions, after major events, on pause menu. Auto-save timer (every 5-10 min). Rotating slots (3 auto-saves). Prevent save during combat. Async save to avoid frame spikes.

CI/CD for Games: Automated build pipeline: trigger on commit, build for all platforms, run tests, upload artifacts. Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI. Perforce/Git LFS for large binary assets.

# GitHub Actions game build workflow
name: Build & Deploy
on: push to main
jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: lfs: true
      - name: Build
        run: |
          if runner.os == 'Windows'; then
            .\build.bat -platform=Win64
          else
            ./build.sh -platform=${{ runner.os == 'macOS' ? 'Mac' : 'Linux' }}
          fi
      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: game-${{ runner.os }}
          path: build/
Platform-Specific Builds: Windows: MSVC, DirectX, Steamworks. macOS: Metal, App Bundle, notarization. Linux: Vulkan/OpenGL, AppImage/Flatpak. Console: Xbox GDK, PS5 SDK, Switch NX. Mobile: Android AAB, iOS IPA.
Asset Building & Cooking: Cook assets: convert source (PNG, FBX, WAV) to runtime format (DDS, mesh, Ogg). Deterministic builds. Dependency graph for incremental building. Asset bundles for patching.
Content Patching & DLC: Binary patching: bsdiff, Courgette for executables. Asset bundles for new content. Patch size minimization: chunk-based downloads. Steamworks UGC (User-Generated Content). Modding support.
Steam & Console Integration: Steamworks SDK: achievements, leaderboards, friends, cloud saves, matchmaking, DRM. Console SDKs: Xbox Live, PSN, Nintendo Switch Online. Cross-platform accounts and progression.
Crash Reporting & Telemetry: Crash reporters: Crashpad (Chrome), Google Breakpad, Unity Cloud Diagnostics. Symbolication for native crashes. Telemetry: frame rate, memory usage, heat maps. GDPR compliance for player data.

Color Blindness Modes: 8% of males have color vision deficiency. Modes: Protanopia (red-blind), Deuteranopia (green-blind), Tritanopia (blue-blind). Use patterns/shapes/icons in addition to color. Simulate in dev tools.
Subtitle Systems: Dialogue subtitles, sound effect captions, directional indicators (who is speaking). Timed text with character-by-character reveal. Closed captions for cutscenes. Accessibility: font size, background opacity.
Text Localization (i18n): Separate text from code. Locale files (JSON, YAML, PO). Placeholders for dynamic values. Pluralization rules (gettext ICU). RTL languages: Arabic, Hebrew. Font fallback for CJK characters.
Font Rendering & Text Layout: Bitmap fonts (sprite sheets) vs Signed Distance Field (SDF). SDF: resolution-independent, glow/shadow effects. TrueType/OpenType rendering: FreeType, HarfBuzz for complex scripts. Kerning, ligatures.
Input Remapping & Accessibility: Full control remapping UI. Hold/toggle options. Slow mode (game speed reduction). Auto-aim assistance. Single-switch input for motor disabilities. Speech-to-text for voice commands.
Difficulty Options & Assist Modes: Granular difficulty sliders: enemy damage, health, speed, AI reaction time. Invulnerability mode. Infinite ammo. Skip puzzle option. Checkpoint frequency. Celeste-style assist mode inspires inclusion.

GDScript Deep: Godot's primary scripting language. Dynamically typed with optional typing. Signals as first-class citizens. Features: match statements, @onready, @export, static typing, lambda functions.
C# in Godot: Godot supports C# via .NET. Full access to engine API, async/await, LINQ, third-party libraries. Scene scripts in C#. Slightly slower iteration than GDScript but better tooling and performance.
Scene Tree & Nodes: Every Godot project is a tree of nodes. Scenes are reusable node subtrees. Access via $ notation (get_node). Node lifecycle: _enter_tree, _ready, _process, _exit_tree. Groups and signals enable decoupling.
Signals & Groups: Signals are Godot's event system: type-safe, built-in or custom. Connect via editor or code with bind/flags. Groups tag nodes for bulk operations. Alternative to tight coupling.

extends Node

signal health_changed(old_value: int, new_value: int)
signal died()

func take_damage(amount: int) -> void:
    var old = health
    health -= amount
    if health <= 0:
        health = 0
        died.emit()
    health_changed.emit(old, health)

func _ready():
    # Connect with one-shot
    health_changed.connect(_on_health_changed, CONNECT_ONE_SHOT)
    # Groups
    add_to_group("enemies")
    # Call on all group members
    get_tree().call_group("enemies", "pause")
    # Get all group nodes
    var enemies = get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemies")
Tilemaps & TileSets: TileMapLayer node for grid-based levels. TileSet resource defines tiles with physics, navigation, terrain (auto-tiling). Custom data layers per tile. Animated and random tiles.

extends TileMapLayer

func _ready():
    # Create tileset programmatically
    var tileset = TileSet.new()
    var source = TileSetAtlasSource.new()
    source.texture = preload("res://tileset.png")
    source.texture_region_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
    tileset.add_source(source)
    
    # Set tile at coordinates
    set_cell(Vector2i(5, 3), 0, Vector2i(0, 0))
    
    # Terrain (auto-tiling)
    # Set terrain bits per corner for automatic connections
    set_cells_terrain_connect(get_used_cells(), 0, 0)
Animation Player & AnimationTree: AnimationPlayer: keyframe animation for any node property. AnimationTree: state machine blending with parameters. Blend spaces (1D/2D). Root motion for animation-driven movement.
Particles & Shaders: GPUParticles2D/3D for high-performance particle systems. Particle shaders control emission, velocity, color over lifetime. CanvasItem shaders for 2D, Spatial for 3D. VisualShaders for node-based editing.
Multiplayer & Export: Godot's high-level multiplayer API: scene replication, RPCs (remote procedure calls), authority modes. Export presets for Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS, Web. Autoloads for persistent singletons.
Input Map & Actions: Godot's Input Map defines named actions (move_left, jump) bound to keys/buttons. Access via Input singleton. Action strength for analog input. Input events vs polling. Input processing order.
Resources & Resource System: Resources are reusable data containers (.tres, .res). Built-in vs external resources. Custom resources for game data (items, stats, dialogue). Resource cache and preloading.
Editor Plugins & @tool Scripts: @tool scripts run in the editor for live preview, custom gizmos, inspector plugins. EditorPlugin for adding docks, buttons, menus. Build custom importers, exporters, and level editors.

tool
 extends EditorPlugin

const MainDock = preload("res://addons/my_tool/dock.tscn")
var dock_instance: Control

func _enter_tree() -> void:
    # Add custom button to toolbar
    add_tool_menu_item("Generate Level", Callable(self, "_generate_level"))
    
    # Add dock to editor
    dock_instance = MainDock.instantiate()
    add_control_to_dock(DOCK_SLOT_LEFT_UR, dock_instance)
    
    # Custom inspector plugin
    var inspector_plugin = preload("res://addons/my_tool/item_inspector_plugin.gd").new()
    add_inspector_plugin(inspector_plugin)

func _exit_tree() -> void:
    remove_tool_menu_item("Generate Level")
    remove_control_from_docks(dock_instance)
    dock_instance.queue_free()
GDExtension & C++ Bindings: GDExtension (Godot 4): dynamically link C++ libraries without recompiling engine. Full performance for compute-heavy systems. Bind classes, expose to GDScript. Replace GDNative from Godot 3.
Godot XR Tools: Godot XR: OpenXR integration for VR/AR. XROrigin3D, XRCamera3D, XRController3D nodes. Hand tracking, passthrough AR. Optimized for standalone headsets (Quest, Pico). XR-specific shaders and performance.
Godot 4 Render Modes: Godot 4 offers 3 renderers: Forward+ (desktop, many lights, SSAO, glow), Mobile (faster, no SSAO, simpler), Compatibility (OpenGL 3.3 / GLES 3.0 fallback). Switch per-platform in Project Settings.

# Project Settings → Rendering → Renderer
# Options: forward_plus, mobile, gl_compatibility

# RenderingDevice singleton for advanced GPU operations
func setup_forward_plus():
    # Full glow & SSAO
    get_viewport().use_taa = true
    get_viewport().scaling_3d_scale = 0.75  # FSR upscaling

func setup_mobile():
    # Limit lights for performance
    RenderingServer.directional_soft_shadow_filter_set_quality(
        RenderingServer.SHADOW_QUALITY_HARD)
    RenderingServer.positional_soft_shadow_filter_set_quality(
        RenderingServer.SHADOW_QUALITY_HARD)

# Query current renderer
func get_renderer_name() -> String:
    match RenderingServer.get_rendering_device().get_device_name():
        var name: return "Forward+ (" + name + ")"
        _: return "Compatibility"
